notes: The positive-and-negative control in one query: `id` and `text` are declared NOT NULL and must stay NOT NULL, while `owner_id` has no constraint and must stay nullable. `LIMIT 1` is semantically inert for nullability -- it can only remove rows, never introduce NULLs -- so it is here to check that a row-count-modifying clause does not perturb the answer. An engine that blanket-degrades to nullable would fail the first two columns; one that trusts a sampled row would wrongly call `owner_id` NOT NULL.
